bundleBudgetNote: 30 KB gzip per route entry chunk (dist/.vite/manifest.json's file for that route's source, e.g. src/routes/FriendsRoute.tsx; the shared framework chunk and any component shared by both routes, e.g. Modal.tsx, are split into their own chunk by Rollup's default dynamic-import handling and are not counted against either route). Measured on this machine: the clean baseline's own two route chunks are 3.02 KB (friends, grown from 2.44 KB after the masonry image feed extension) and 1.47 KB (party) gzip, docs/bundle_baseline_measurement.txt. 30 KB is roughly 15 to 20x that, real headroom for a route to grow a genuine feature, while every one of the 8 seeded bundle regressions measured between 45.25 KB (moment.js with 4 locales, the smallest) and 185.15 KB (inlined base64 avatars, the largest) gzip, comfortably over it; see docs/bundle_regression_sizes.txt for the full measured table. This mirrors a real route-level JS budget a frontend team would set for a single feature area (not the whole app) that should stay fast on a mid-tier phone.
virtualizationNote: The check always requests the image feed (route slug /friends, see FriendsRoute.tsx) with exactly 10,000 entries via ?count=10000, regardless of a variant's own default display count, scrolls its scroll container to the midpoint, and counts mounted [data-feed-item] tiles there, so every variant is checked against the same worst case and the same steady-state scroll position (not the top edge, where there is nothing above to overscan into). The feed is a 7-column masonry grid (masonryLayout.ts), tile heights 90 to 180px, inside a 640px fixed-height scroll container, with a 1,050px pixel-based overscan each side (roughly 1.6 viewport-heights, larger than the row list's 10-row overscan because an image tile benefits from more preload than a text row). Measured on this machine at the feed's midpoint: a correct implementation mounts roughly 142 to 147 tiles across repeated runs (docs/virtualization_measurement.txt has the exact runs). 400 is set with real headroom above that (for a slightly different scroll position or a taller viewport) and far below 10,000, so it cannot be crossed by a correct implementation and cannot be missed by a broken one that renders the full feed.
virtualizeAtListLengthNote: Below this the app renders every tile directly (no windowing machinery needed for a short feed); at or above it the app switches to windowed masonry rendering. This only affects the app's own default behavior at small sizes; the gate's virtualization check always forces 10,000 entries via the count override above.
focusNote: Tabs through every focusable element on the loaded route from the top (bounded by a maximum tab count so a broken page cannot hang the check), asserting document.activeElement is never document.body mid-sequence, then runs a scripted interaction for every stable [data-focus-trigger] control found on the page (modal open/close, dropdown select, message button activation, nav navigation, search clear), asserting focus lands somewhere sane afterward, never document.body.
